Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings: Known chronic heart failure with recent progressive dyspnea and new bilateral ankle edema. Vitals stable on exam. No chest pain, fever, or palpitations.  

Working diagnosis: Acute decompensated congestive heart failure (high likelihood).  

Differential diagnoses considered  
• Acute decompensated heart failure – high likelihood; history of HF, volume overload signs.  
• Lower-respiratory tract infection precipitating HF – moderate likelihood; mild dry cough, feeling run-down but afebrile and clear chest exam.  
• Pulmonary embolism – low-moderate likelihood; sedentary occupation, acute subjective worsening but lacks typical PE features.

Management Plan

• Increase Furosemide to one tablet twice daily for several days; reassess response.  
• Arrange blood tests: CBC (rule out anemia), renal function/electrolytes (monitor diuretic effect).  
• Order echocardiogram to assess current cardiac function.  
• Review in 1 week; earlier contact advised for worsening breathlessness, chest pain, palpitations, or dizziness.  
• Education: explained possible HF flare, medication adjustment, and need for monitoring.

- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits):  Not recorded.  
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral:  Not recorded.  
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support):  Not recorded.  
- CTG registration:  Not recorded.  
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test):  Follow-up appointment in 1 week booked; other preventive care not recorded.  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):

1. Acute decompensated congestive heart failure – High likelihood: known HF plus dyspnea and peripheral edema.  
2. Lower-respiratory tract infection – Moderate likelihood: concurrent dry cough/run-down feeling; may precipitate HF exacerbation.  
3. Pulmonary embolism – Low-moderate likelihood: sedentary lorry driving; acute worsening, but lacks classic PE signs.
